title: GTA 7 new city: Rockstar won't rule out leaving America
description: GTA 7 new city talk heats up as Rockstar North's Rob Nelson says 'never say never' on leaving America, according to Dexerto. Here is what we know.

body.text: The GTA 7 new city question has a fresh talking point: according to Dexerto, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson has left the door open to a Grand Theft Auto game set somewhere new, possibly outside the United States. Nothing is confirmed, and GTA 7 has not been announced, but the comments matter because the series has spent decades circling the same American locations.

Dexerto reports that Nelson was speaking to The Guardian when he was asked if Rockstar could picture a GTA game outside the US. His answer was "never say never", followed by the point that there is still plenty left to explore in America.

That is not a promise. Nelson did not mention GTA 7 by name, and he did not say Rockstar plans to leave American settings behind. Dexerto's reading is that the series may stay in the US but could still move to a fresh location within it.

According to Dexerto, GTA 6 launches on November 19, taking players back to Vice City, Rockstar's take on Miami, and the wider state of Leonida. For Indian players counting down to launch, that means another return to a familiar name.
The franchise has long rotated through Liberty City, Los Santos and Vice City. That repetition is why fans keep asking whether a later game could break the pattern.
GTA 7 new city: the scrapped overseas ideas

Dexerto notes that Rockstar has looked abroad before. Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij has said GTA: Tokyo was seriously considered, with a Japanese developer potentially leading it.

The case for staying in America

Vermeij was far less hopeful about the series leaving the US when he discussed GTA's future in January 2026, according to Dexerto. He argued that Rockstar is effectively stuck with American cities because their familiarity and cultural pull make them safer picks for games with enormous budgets.
Nelson's remarks sit differently from that view. They do not contradict it outright, but they suggest the studio has not fully closed off the idea of somewhere different.

For now, Rockstar's focus is GTA 6, which Dexerto says has taken more than a decade to develop and offers the series' most detailed version of America so far. A former Rockstar developer has suggested GTA 7 may already be in development, but that is unconfirmed, and the studio has not announced the next game or where it might be set. Until Rockstar says more, treat any GTA 7 location talk, including claims about leaks, as speculation. The next real signal will likely come after GTA 6 is out and players see how the studio follows it up.

sources.title: GTA 7 could finally introduce a completely new city as Rockstar opens door to leaving America
